theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: Why must a salon or spa worker know the products and services the business sells?
options: To answer clients' questions and give honest advice
To sell the most costly item to every client who comes in
To avoid asking clients any questions about their needs
To tell clients that a product will cure a skin disease

questions.stem: Where is the best place to find correct facts about a product's ingredients and how to use it?
options: From what other clients have said about it on social media
From the label, the maker's leaflet and the salon's training
From a guess based on the colour and smell of the product
From the price, since dearer products always have better ingredients

questions.stem: A client asks what is in a facial serum, and you do not know. What should you do?
options: Say it is all natural so she will not worry
Change the subject quickly and talk about a different product
Say you will check, then read the label or ask a senior
Tell her to buy it first and read the box at home

questions.stem: What is a "feature" of a product?
options: What the product does for the client, such as giving softer, shinier hair
The reason the client came into the salon on that day
The discount the salon gives when a client buys two items
A fact about the product itself, such as its size or ingredients

questions.stem: Which of these is a "benefit" to the client, not a feature?
options: The shampoo comes in a 500 ml bottle
The body cream contains shea butter, cocoa butter and aloe vera
The nail polish is sold in twelve colours
The conditioner leaves dry hair soft and easy to comb

questions.stem: A sunscreen has SPF 30. How would you explain its benefit to a client?
options: It is the most popular sunscreen sold in Jamaica this year
It means you can stay in strong sun all day and never burn at all
It helps protect your skin from sunburn when you are outdoors
It has the number 30 printed on the front of the tube

questions.stem: Which of these is an "open" question, one that gets the client to talk about her needs?
options: How do you care for your hair at home?
Do you like the shampoo you use at home now?
Is your skin oily?
Would you like to buy this today?

questions.stem: What is the main reason to ask questions and listen before you recommend a product?
options: To keep the client talking until the service is finished
To find out what the client needs, so you suggest the right item
To learn private facts about the client's family and money
To make the consultation last as long as possible so the bill is higher

questions.stem: During a consultation, Mrs Reid says her hair breaks easily. What should you do next?
options: Sell her the biggest tub of hair food that the salon has in stock
Tell her that broken hair is normal and nothing can be done
Book her for a relaxer straight away to make the hair stronger
Ask how she styles and treats her hair, and look at its condition

questions.stem: In selling, what is a "buying signal"?
options: A sign on the shelf that shows the price and the offer on each item
The beep the till makes when a sale goes through
Something the client says or does that shows they want to buy
A message the supplier sends when new stock is ready

questions.stem: Which of these is a buying signal from a client?
options: She picks up the tester, smells it and asks the price
She checks her phone and says she must leave soon
She walks past the shelf without looking at it
She says she already has plenty of that product at home

questions.stem: After a relaxer service, which product is the most suitable to recommend for home care?
options: A strong clarifying shampoo for use every day of the week
A gentle shampoo and conditioner for chemically treated hair
A deep-cleansing face scrub to use on the scalp each night
A home lightening kit to use on the new growth at the roots

questions.stem: A client has just had a manicure. Which product links best to this service?
options: A hair serum
A pumice stone
A cuticle oil
A face mask

questions.stem: What is "link selling" (also called linked selling)?
options: Selling only to clients who already have a loyalty card
Selling products by sending web links to clients on social media
Asking another salon nearby to sell your products for you
Suggesting an item that goes with what the client is having

questions.stem: Shanice is booked for a pedicure at a day spa. Which extra service links best with her pedicure?
options: A scalp treatment for dandruff
A paraffin wax foot treatment
A relaxer touch-up on the edges
An eyebrow shape with tweezers

questions.stem: A client says she cannot afford a product today. What is the professional thing to do?
options: Thank her, give her a sample or leaflet, and leave it there
Keep telling her about it again and again until she agrees
Tell her the price will go up a lot if she waits
Put the product in her bag and add it to the bill

questions.stem: What does "upselling" mean?
options: Putting the products on the highest shelf in the salon
Raising the prices of all services at the end of the year
Selling stock that is past its use-by date at a lower price than usual
Offering a better or larger version of what the client is buying

questions.stem: A spa sells a "Relax Package": a massage and a facial together, for less than the two cost on their own. What is this called?
options: A gift voucher
A deposit
A package deal
A float

questions.stem: A conditioner normally costs J$2,400. This week it is 25% off. What is the sale price?
A salon offers "buy two styling gels, get the third one free". Each gel is J$950. How much does a client pay for three?
Why are testers (sample bottles) put on a retail display?
options: So staff can use them up during services in the salon
So the display looks full when the stock is running low
So clients can take them home free if they want to
So clients can try the smell and feel before they buy

questions.stem: What is the hygienic way to let clients try a cream tester?
options: Let each client dip a finger straight into the open jar
Use a clean single-use spatula or a pump bottle
Leave the lid off so the cream is easy to reach
Wipe the top of the jar with a tissue once a week

questions.stem: Which display is most likely to help sales?
options: A dusty shelf with products in no order behind the till
Products stacked high in their boxes so clients cannot see the labels
Items placed in direct sunlight in the shop window all day
Clean, well-lit shelves with prices shown and items easy to reach

questions.stem: Why should beauty products not be displayed in a hot, sunny shop window?
options: Heat and sunlight can spoil products and fade the labels
Clients do not like to look at products in a window
Products in a window are always stolen within a day
Sunlight makes the products cost more to buy from the supplier

questions.stem: How often should a retail display be checked, cleaned and topped up?
options: Only when the supplier sends a new delivery
Once a year, at the stock take
Regularly, such as every day before the salon opens
Only when a client complains that the shelf is dusty or empty

questions.stem: A client asks if a cream will remove her stretch marks for good. The maker makes no such claim. What should you say?
options: Yes, it removes all stretch marks in about two weeks
It may help the skin feel softer, but it will not remove them
Yes, but only if she buys three jars at the same time
Yes, every one of our clients says it worked very well for them

questions.stem: Why must you never make false claims about a product?
options: False claims make the product cost more to stock
Clients never believe anything that salon staff tell them anyway
The supplier will not deliver to a salon that does so
It misleads the client, breaks consumer law and harms trust

questions.stem: A client tells you she is allergic to nuts. She wants to buy a body butter. What should you do first?
options: Tell her that body butters never contain any nuts at all
Sell it to her and tell her to stop if her skin starts to itch
Check the ingredients list for nut oils, such as almond oil
Give her the larger size so she gets better value for money

questions.stem: A client opens a new shampoo at home and finds it has gone bad. She brings it back with her receipt. What should happen?
options: Offer a replacement or refund, following the salon's policy
Refuse, because the bottle has been opened
Tell her to take the problem up with the maker by herself
Give her a different, cheaper product that she did not ask for

questions.stem: Why should prices be clearly shown on products and on the service price list?
options: So staff can change the price for each client
So the salon does not need to give any receipts to clients
So the supplier can see what the salon charges
So clients know the cost before they agree to buy

questions.stem: What is an "objection" in selling?
options: A complaint form that the client fills in after a service
A product that the salon has stopped selling because of poor sales
A reason the client gives for not buying yet, such as price
A rule that stops staff from selling to friends

questions.stem: A client says, "That serum is too dear." What is a good way to reply?
options: Tell her that she cannot have nice hair if she will not pay
Explain how long it lasts and show a smaller, cheaper size
Agree it is dear and say nobody really buys it
Ignore what she said and keep talking about the colour

questions.stem: A client says she wants to think about buying a skin care set. What should you do?
options: Respect this, write the items down and invite her back
Tell her the offer ends in five minutes so she must decide now
Follow her out to the car park, still talking about the set
Say that she will regret it if she does not buy it today

questions.stem: What does "closing the sale" mean?
options: Locking the shop door at the end of the day
Taking a product off the shelf because it is no longer sold
Ending the consultation quickly before the client can ask any questions
Getting the client's agreement to buy and completing the payment

questions.stem: Which is a polite way to close a sale?
options: "You have to take this one, it is the last one we have."
"Everybody else in Mandeville buys it, so you should buy it too."
"Shall I put the shampoo and the conditioner with your bill?"
"I will be in trouble with my boss if you do not buy it."

questions.stem: After a client buys a product, what should you tell her?
options: That she cannot return it for any reason at all
How to use it, how much to use and how to store it
How much profit the salon makes on each item sold
Which other clients have bought the same product

questions.stem: Why is it useful to note the products a client buys on her client record?
options: So staff can follow up, give advice and suggest refills
So the salon can share her details with other businesses
So she can be charged more on her next visit
So the record card is full and looks busy

questions.stem: Two weeks after a client buys a new skin care set, the therapist calls her, as she agreed, to ask how it is working. What is this called?
options: A stock take
A cash-up
A walk-in
A follow-up

questions.stem: The salon sets each stylist a target of J$30,000 in product sales this month. Tanisha has sold J$22,500. How much more must she sell to reach the target?
Why does a salon keep a record of its product and service sales?
options: To find out which clients pay with cash
To see what sells well, plan stock and measure targets
To show the records to every client who asks
To decide which member of staff should do the cleaning each day

questions.stem: Some salons pay staff "commission" on sales. What is commission?
options: A fine taken from wages when a client complains
A tax the salon pays to the government on each sale
A gift voucher given to regular clients each year on their birthday
An extra payment, often a part of the sales the worker makes

questions.stem: A client asks about a service the salon offers. Which facts should you be able to tell her?
options: What it involves, how long it takes and what it costs
The names and phone numbers of the last five clients who had it
How much the staff member is paid to do the service
Only the price, as clients do not need other details

questions.stem: When you suggest a chemical service such as a hair colour or a lash tint, what must you tell the client?
options: That the service can be done on any client at any time
That colour and tint products never cause a reaction
That a skin (patch) test is needed first, often 48 hours before
That she must first buy a full colour kit to take home and try on herself

questions.stem: A client asks you about a nail product. You are a hair stylist, and the nail technician knows more. What should you do?
options: Guess the answer so that the client is not kept waiting long
Introduce the client to the nail technician to advise her
Tell the client nail products are not your problem
Tell the client to look the product up on the internet

questions.stem: Why does a worker's own appearance matter when selling beauty products?
options: Clients trust advice from a person who is neat and well groomed
Workers who look smart are allowed to charge higher prices
Appearance does not matter, only the price of the product
Clients only buy products they can see the worker using on herself

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What do the letters SPF stand for on a sunscreen?
What is the name of the tax that is added to the price of most goods and services sold in Jamaica?
A face cream costs J$3,200. A client buys two. What is the total before tax, in J$?
A hair oil costs J$1,500 and is 20% off. How much is taken off the price, in J$?
What paper should a client bring back with a faulty product, to show where and when she bought it?
What do we call the date printed on a product after which it should not be sold or used?
Products sold to clients for home use are retail products. What are the products staff use on clients during services called?
Which product should a client put on her hair before she uses a flat iron, to help protect it from heat damage?
What is the last coat of nail polish called, the one that adds shine and helps stop the colour chipping?
What do we call a small free amount of a product given to a client to try at home?
What is the name of the sheet from the maker that gives a product's hazards, safe storage and first aid?
Which government body in Jamaica can a shopper contact about unfair selling or faulty goods?
Which skin type looks shiny all over and has large, open pores?
A client pays with J$5,000 for products that cost J$4,350. How much change should she get, in J$?
What is the printed list of all the services and their prices, shown at the reception desk, usually called?

essays.stem: Choose one hair product and one skin or nail product that a salon or spa might sell. For each one, give two features and explain the benefit each feature brings to the client.
essays.modelAnswer: A feature is a fact about the product. A benefit is what that fact does for the client. Hair product: a leave-in conditioner. Feature 1: it contains coconut oil. Benefit: it helps keep dry or relaxed hair soft and less likely to break. Feature 2: it comes in a spray bottle. Benefit: it is quick to use each morning and spreads evenly without making the hair greasy. Skin product: a facial sunscreen with SPF 30. Feature 1: SPF 30. Benefit: it helps protect the face from sunburn and dark marks when the client is out in the Jamaican sun. Feature 2: it is oil-free. Benefit: it does not leave oily skin shiny or block the pores, so the client is happy to wear it every day. When I sell, I say the benefit in words that link to what the client told me in the consultation.
markingPoints: Shows that a feature is a fact about the product and a benefit is what it does for the client
Two correct features, each with its benefit, for a hair product
Two correct features, each with its benefit, for a skin or nail product
Links the benefits to the client's own needs

essays.stem: Describe how you would find out a client's needs before you recommend products for her to use at home.
essays.modelAnswer: I would greet the client warmly and explain that I want to suggest the right home care for her. I would look at her client record to see her past services, the products she has bought and any allergies. Then I would ask open questions, such as "How do you care for your skin at home?" and "What would you like to change?" I would listen carefully without interrupting, and repeat the main points back to check that I understood. I would look at the hair, skin or nails to judge the type and condition, for example dry ends, an oily T-zone or dry cuticles. I would also ask about her budget, how much time she has for a routine, and any allergies or skin problems. Only then would I suggest one or two products that match what she told me, explain why, and note the advice on her record.
markingPoints: Checks the client record for past services, purchases and allergies
Uses open questions about her home care and what she wants
Listens and checks understanding by repeating the main points
Looks at the hair, skin or nails to judge type and condition
Asks about budget, time and allergies before recommending, and records the advice

essays.stem: Describe the main steps of selling a product to a client, from the first greeting to the end of the sale.
essays.modelAnswer: First I greet the client with a smile, use her name and make her feel welcome, so that she is relaxed and trusts me. Next I find out her needs by asking open questions, listening and looking at her hair, skin or nails. Then I present one or two suitable products. I explain the features and the benefits for her, and let her try a tester using a clean spatula or pump. If she has a concern, such as the price, I listen and answer it honestly, for example by showing a smaller size. When she shows buying signals, I close the sale by asking politely if she would like to take it today. I take the payment, give a receipt and explain how to use and store the product. Finally I note the sale on her record, thank her, and invite her to come back or call if she has questions.
markingPoints: Greets the client and builds rapport
Finds her needs with questions, listening and looking
Presents suitable products with features and benefits, and uses testers hygienically
Deals with concerns politely and closes by asking for the sale
Takes payment, gives a receipt and use advice, records the sale and thanks the client

essays.stem: A client likes a hair treatment you suggest, but says it is too dear. Explain how you would deal with this, and why you must not pressure her.
essays.modelAnswer: I would listen to her without arguing and accept that price matters to her. Then I would explain the value: for example, that one bottle lasts about two months, so it costs only a little each week, and that it will help with the dryness she told me about. I would offer her a choice, such as a smaller size, a cheaper product that still suits her hair, a free sample to try, or buying it on her next visit. If she still says no, I accept her answer politely and note her interest on her record so I can mention it another time. I must not pressure her, because pushing a client makes her feel uncomfortable and she may not come back. Pressure also damages trust in the salon and can be unfair selling. A happy client who buys later is worth more than one forced sale.
markingPoints: Listens and accepts the concern without arguing
Explains the value: how long it lasts and the benefit she wants
Offers a choice: a smaller size, a cheaper item, a sample or a later date
Accepts her decision politely and notes her interest for later
Explains that pressure harms trust and repeat business and can be unfair selling

essays.stem: Explain why salon and spa staff must sell honestly. In your answer, describe the rights a client has when she buys products and services.
essays.modelAnswer: Staff must sell honestly because clients trust their advice about what goes on their hair, skin and nails. A client has the right to true information, so staff must never claim that a product cures a condition or gives results the maker does not promise. She has the right to know the full price before she agrees, so prices must be clearly shown, with GCT added at the current rate as the law and the salon's policy require. She has the right to a receipt, and to a refund, repair or replacement if a product is faulty or not as described, following the salon's policy and consumer law. She has the right to safe, in-date goods, with correct advice on use, allergies and storage. Honest selling keeps the salon within the law, avoids complaints and builds trust, so clients come back and recommend the business.
markingPoints: Gives true facts and makes no false claims about results
Shows clear prices, with GCT added as the law and policy require
Gives a receipt and follows the refund or exchange policy for faulty goods
Sells only safe, in-date products and gives correct use and allergy advice
Explains that honest selling keeps within consumer law and builds trust

essays.stem: Describe how to set up and keep a retail display in a salon or spa so that it is clean, safe and attractive.
essays.modelAnswer: I would choose a place clients can see, such as near reception, but out of direct sun and heat and clear of walkways and the fire exit. I would clean the shelves and wipe each product before setting it out. Heavy items and glass bottles go on the lower shelves so they cannot fall. I would group products by type or need, for example hair care, skin care and nail care, with labels facing forward and a clear price ticket on each. Testers would be pump bottles or used with clean single-use spatulas, and marked as testers. I would put older stock at the front so it sells first. Every day before opening I would check the display, dust it, fill gaps and take away any damaged, leaking or out-of-date products, and record them. A tidy, well-lit display with clear prices helps clients choose and buy.
markingPoints: Chooses a safe place out of direct sun and clear of walkways and exits
Cleans the shelves and products, with heavy and glass items low and steady
Groups products sensibly, labels facing out, with clear price tickets
Keeps testers hygienic and puts older stock at the front
Checks, cleans and refills regularly and removes damaged or out-of-date stock

essays.stem: Explain how you would recommend extra services and home-care products that link to the service a client is having. Give one example from a hair salon and one from a spa or nail bar.
essays.modelAnswer: Link selling means suggesting a product or service that goes with what the client is already having. I would base each suggestion on what I learnt in the consultation, not just on what I want to sell. I would explain the benefit to her in plain words and let her decide. In a hair salon, a client having a relaxer touch-up has told me her ends are dry. I could suggest a deep conditioning treatment while she is at the basin, and a gentle shampoo and leave-in conditioner for chemically treated hair to use at home. In a spa, a client having a pedicure has dry, cracked heels. I could suggest adding a paraffin wax foot treatment, and a foot cream to use each night. If she says no, I accept it politely. Honest link selling helps the client get a better result and raises the salon's sales.
markingPoints: Explains link selling: suggesting items that go with the service
Bases suggestions on the client's needs found in the consultation
Gives a suitable hair salon example
Gives a suitable spa or nail example
Explains the benefit honestly and accepts the client's answer

essays.stem: Before you sell a product or book a service that could cause a skin reaction, such as a hair colour, a lash tint or a body scrub, what must you check and tell the client? Explain why.
essays.modelAnswer: First I would check her client record and ask about allergies, sensitive skin, skin problems and any medical conditions or medicines that could matter. I would read the ingredients and the maker's instructions for the product. I would look at the skin or scalp for cuts, sores, rashes, irritation or recent sunburn. If I find any of these, the service must not go ahead, and I would advise her to see a doctor. For tints and colours, I would book a skin (patch) test as the maker requires, often 48 hours before the service, and note the result on her record. I would tell her what a reaction looks like, such as redness, itching or swelling, and to rinse the product off and get medical advice if it happens. These checks protect the client from harm, and show that the salon has taken proper care.
markingPoints: Asks about allergies, sensitive skin and medical conditions, and checks the record
Reads the ingredients and follows the maker's instructions
Checks the skin or scalp for cuts, irritation or infection, does not treat and refers to a doctor if found
Books a skin test as the maker requires (often 48 hours before) and records the result
Explains this protects the client from harm and shows the salon took proper care

essays.stem: Explain why a salon keeps records of the products and services it sells, and how these records help the business and its clients.
essays.modelAnswer: Sales records show the owner which products and services sell well and which sell slowly. This helps the salon plan its stock, so it orders enough of the popular lines and does not waste money on items that sit on the shelf until they expire. The records also show whether each staff member is reaching the sales target, and they are used to work out any commission. For clients, a note on the client record of what they bought helps staff to give good advice next time, remind them when a refill is due, and avoid suggesting a product that caused a problem or an allergy before. Records also help if a client brings back a faulty product. All records must be accurate, kept up to date and kept private, so that client details are never shared without permission.
markingPoints: Shows which products and services sell well or slowly
Helps plan stock orders, avoiding running out or overstocking
Tracks sales against targets and works out commission
Client purchase notes support advice, refills and follow-up, and flag allergies
Records are accurate, up to date and kept private

essays.stem: A day spa has many jars of a body scrub that are selling slowly. Describe how the staff could plan and run a promotion to sell them.
essays.modelAnswer: First the staff would check that the jars are in date and in good condition, and agree a goal, for example to sell 20 jars in four weeks. Next they would choose a fair offer, such as a small discount, a bundle with a body lotion, or a free mini scrub with every body treatment. They would build an eye-catching display near reception, with a clean tester used by spatula, and clear signs giving the offer, the price and the end date. Every therapist would learn the features and benefits of the scrub and how it links to body treatments, so they can suggest it honestly during consultations. The spa could post the offer on its social media page and send messages to clients who have agreed to receive them. At the end, the staff would count the sales against the goal and decide whether to repeat the offer.
markingPoints: Checks the stock is in date and sets a goal and a time
Chooses a fair offer, such as a discount, a bundle or a free sample with a service
Builds a clear display with signs, prices and a hygienic tester
Trains staff on features, benefits and linking the product to services
Advertises to clients who agreed, and checks the results at the end

practical1.title: Consultation and sale role play: recommend home-care products
practical1.brief: As a group, run a series of short selling role plays in the Centre's salon reception. The assessor gives each member a client card, for example: dry relaxed hair that breaks; oily skin and open pores; dry cuticles after a manicure; skin that is often out in the sun; a client who says the price is too high. Take turns so that every member plays the seller once and the client once, while another member keeps notes and a fourth takes the photos. As the seller, greet the client, find her needs with open questions, recommend one or two suitable products from the salon's stock, explain the features and benefits, let her try a tester hygienically, deal with any concern and close the sale politely. Then fill in a product recommendation sheet and a sales slip in J$, showing the price of each item, any discount and GCT at the rate the assessor gives. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Photos show hands, products and paperwork, not faces. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: A range of salon and spa retail products and testers (hair, skin and nail care)
Single-use spatulas, tissues and hand sanitiser
Product recommendation sheets and sales slips
Price list in J$, and a calculator
Pens and a clipboard for the note-taker
photos: The products and testers set out, with prices showing
Each seller showing a product to the client (hands and product only)
A tester being used with a clean spatula or pump
Each member's completed product recommendation sheet
Each member's completed sales slip with the J$ total
The note-taker's notes for each role play
checklist: Greeted the client politely and built rapport
Used open questions and listened to find the client's needs
Recommended products that suit the needs on the client card
Explained features and benefits clearly and honestly, with no false claims
Used testers hygienically and asked about allergies before any product touched the skin
Dealt with a concern or objection politely, without pressure
Closed the sale politely, or accepted the client's decision
Filled in the recommendation sheet and the sales slip correctly, with the right J$ total
safety: Ask about allergies first; do not apply a tester to broken, sore or irritated skin
Use a clean single-use spatula for each tester; never double-dip
Keep products away from the eyes; rinse with clean water if any gets in
Wash or sanitise hands before and after handling testers
Keep the reception area tidy, with no bags or boxes in the walkway

practical2.title: Plan and build a promotional retail display, and present it to clients
practical2.brief: As a group, plan and build a retail display that promotes a range of products for one client need, for example "Healthy hair after a relaxer", "Sun care for Jamaican skin" or "Soft hands and feet". Choose products that suit both salon and spa clients. First, agree the theme and draw a simple plan of the display. Then clean the shelf or table, and set out the products safely, with heavy and glass items low, labels facing forward and older stock at the front. Make clear price tickets in J$ and one promotion poster that states the offer and its end date. Each member writes a product card for one product, giving two features and their benefits, and then presents that product to a visitor (the assessor or another group) for about 3 minutes and answers one question. At the end, take the display down if asked and leave the area clean. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: A shelf unit or table in the Centre's reception or retail area
Salon and spa retail products and testers from the Centre's stock
Card, markers and a ruler for price tickets, product cards and a poster
Cleaning cloths and a suitable surface cleaner
Plain paper for the display plan
photos: The display plan, with each member's job written on it
The empty shelf or table, cleaned
The finished display from the front
A close view of the price tickets and the promotion poster
Each member presenting a product to the visitor
The area left clean and tidy at the end
checklist: Took part in planning the theme and the layout
Cleaned the area and placed products safely, heavy and glass items low
Placed labels facing forward and older stock at the front
Wrote a correct price ticket or product card with true features and benefits
Presented a product clearly, in plain words, without false claims
Answered the visitor's question politely and correctly
Kept walkways and the fire exit clear
Helped to clear and clean the area at the end
safety: Lift boxes of stock with a straight back and bent knees; ask for help with heavy loads
Use a proper step stool, not a chair, to reach a high shelf
Keep the display clear of walkways, doors and the fire exit
Wipe up any spilled product at once and put out a wet-floor sign
Use cleaning products as the label says, with gloves if needed
